title: Atomic Theme Cascade and Brand Isolation for Console Components
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: introduce an additive 'atomic' token cascade and brand isolation layer so third-party brand themes can be applied to Console components (buttons, tables, charts, and data cards) without wide token collisions. Scope: 1) define atomic.* token namespace and mapping rules (semantic -> atomic mappings), 2) implement component-level override hooks for Button/Table/Chart components, 3) create low-light interpolation path for dark mode brand variants, 4) migration guide and codemod for existing themes. Out of scope: complete overhaul of iconography, new brand themes for customers. Acceptance criteria: - components render identical visual hierarchy across baseline, brand-adapted, and dark-brand modes with token fallbacks - no regressions in automated contrast checks (WCAG AA for text >=14px) - PRs for tokens and component overrides merged and release notes published.

decisions: Use 'atomic.' prefix for additive tokens (e.g. atomic.surface-weak, atomic.accent-muted, atomic.text-on-accent) to avoid collisions with legacy semantic tokens.
Component overrides implemented as small, opt-in hook functions: getBrandOverrides(componentName, brandContext) that return token mappings at render time.
Charts: adopt desaturation-first strategy for brand overlays (reduce saturation by 28% before applying hue shift) to preserve value contrast while reflecting brand color.
Tables: keep zebra rows semantic (stripe.surface-muted) and only apply brand tint to non-critical surfaces; do not tint selection/highlight states to avoid losing affordance.

Fallback policy: mapping resolves in order: brand-specific atomic.* -> base atomic.* -> legacy semantic token -> hard-coded fallback; accessibility contrast adjustments applied at the final resolved color.
Migration approach: release codemod that rewrites theme override objects to the new atomic namespace and emits a migration report per repo.
Scope-limited rollout: start with buttons and simple form controls, then expand to tables and charts after two-week observation window.
